---
title: "About"
---

I'm Anupam Gupta. Online, I go by "Next Door Geek", and sometimes as "mapuna".

This blog continues one I kept at [lifemath.wordpress.com](https://lifemath.wordpress.com/); 
some of the older posts may follow me here.

I run a company... No. I run the tech and research at more than one companies.
Around those, I do research, write code, and teach when someone lets me.

What shows up here: machine learning, information theory, information retrieval,
and the probability, optimization, and combinatorics they run on (cs.LG,
cs.IT and math.IT, cs.IR, math.PR, math.OC, math.CO). What mostly stays in my
notebooks: algebraic geometry and topology, computational complexity and
geometry, cryptography, the theory of data structures (math.AG, math.AT, cs.CC,
cs.CG, cs.CR, cs.DS).

Most posts circle one question. Given a task, what is the least you can store or
transmit and still do the task well? For a photograph shown to a person the task
is perception, and the answer is classical rate-distortion theory. For a
classifier, a detector, or a language model the task is something else, and the
compressed form might feed the model directly, with NO actual modality of the 
input ever reconstructed.
